positions.as_written: Keep the beam perpendicular to the fibres, which is the whole technique.
Follow the tendon along its length and correct the angle as the tendon curves, because a curved tendon cannot be perpendicular everywhere at once.
Confirm in a second plane, where a tear persists and an angle effect does not.
At decision level this page is the reason a tendon tear reported on ultrasound should be confirmed before it is operated on.
